auth.notes: Tuya account + cloud-issued pairing; device-side auth for the BLE session is the device uuid / local key pair issued at pairing.

endpoints.name: Tuya OpenAPI / app API
endpoints.notes: No tuya*.com hostnames appear as plaintext anywhere in the Smart Life app — region endpoints are delivered at runtime by Tuya's config service. The hosts listed are the publicly documented Tuya endpoint families, recorded for orientation.

cloud.failure_mode: Stock firmware is dead without Tuya cloud at PAIRING time: pairing needs a Tuya account (the local key is cloud-issued), and the encrypted session cannot be established without it. Once paired and the device id + local key are extracted, day-to-day local monitoring (ha_tuya_ble / python-tuya-ble over direct BLE) keeps working with the Tuya cloud gone — the sensor never touches Wi-Fi itself. Remote access, Alexa/Google and cloud automations die with the cloud or the optional BLE gateway. The SGS01BTHome replacement firmware removes the cloud dependency entirely (BTHome passive broadcast) for the SGS01 revision.
cloud.notes: The ONLY hard cloud dependency for local use is one-time pairing + key extraction: pair in Smart Life, link the account to a free Tuya IoT developer project, pull device id + local key (tuya-iot-py-sdk / ha_tuya_ble automate this). Tuya has broken this flow for some account types in the past — verify current status before buying hardware for a local-only install. The device UI in the vendor app is a cloud-delivered RN panel: zero hits for `zwjcy` anywhere in the Smart Life app; only the generic BLE transport machinery is in it.
cloud.vendor_service: Tuya cloud (Smart Life / Tuya Smart platform)

dp_query.description: GATT write of a DPS request (0x0002) to 0x2B11; the report arrives as a 0x8001 notification on 0x2B10.

pair.description: GATT write of PAIR frames (0x0001) to characteristic 0x2B11; establishes the encrypted session from device uuid + local key.

discovery.notes: Advertisements are connectable and carry service-data UUID 0xA201 plus Tuya manufacturer data (company ID 0x07D0) with device identity — never sensor values. Confidence: reported (community integrations + the Smart Life BLE SDK), not captured by this project.

manufacturer_data.description: Tuya's Bluetooth SIG company ID 0x07D0, present in the advertisement manufacturer data. Combined with service-data UUID 0xA201 this is how Home Assistant's tuya_ble discovery fingerprints Tuya BLE single-point devices; it identifies "a Tuya BLE device", not this family specifically.

identification.notes: Distinguishing a soil tester from any other Tuya BLE single-point device requires connecting (pairing) and reading device info / DPs, or matching the product id learned at cloud pairing time against `device.variants`.

device.manufacturer: Tuya (platform) / Shenzhen HaiHao Electronic Co., LTD (canonical SGS01) + white-label clones
device.name: Tuya Bluetooth Soil Tester (zwjcy / SGS01 family)
device.notes:
A battery-powered (2×AAA) probe that measures soil moisture and temperature, marketed as "works with Alexa & Google". Internally it is a two-processor device (per the haraldapp/SGS01BTHome teardown): a Tuya BT3L module (Telink TLSR8250, 512 KB flash) runs stock Tuya BLE firmware and owns the radio, while a separate third-party MCU owns the actual measurement, button and LED; the two are linked by UART running the standard Tuya MCU serial protocol (the same frame family as TuyaMCU Wi-Fi devices).
PROTOCOL: this is a Tuya BLE "single-point" device — connectable GATT, NOT BLE mesh and NOT a passive beacon. Advertisements carry device identity only, never sensor readings; the ble_monitor project confirms SGS01 cannot be supported passively. All state moves as encrypted Tuya DP (datapoint) frames over GATT service 0xFD50 (write 0x2B11, notify 0x2B10). The session is encrypted with keys derived from the device's Tuya `uuid` plus the cloud-issued `local_key`, so any local integration first needs the device id + local key from a Tuya IoT cloud account — the same one-time key-extraction step as Tuya Wi-Fi devices.
HUB QUESTION: with the phone nearby, Smart Life talks to the device directly over BLE — no hub needed for in-range monitoring. Remote access, Alexa/Google and cloud automations require a Tuya Bluetooth gateway (or multi-mode ZigBee+BLE gateway) bridging the BLE sub-device to Wi-Fi/cloud; the "works with Alexa" marketing presupposes that gateway. The device cannot be cloud-controlled standalone.
CLOUD-FREE PATH: the BT3L is a Telink TLSR8250 with SWS flashing pads (chip type B85), and haraldapp/SGS01BTHome ships full replacement firmware that turns the sensor into a BTHome v2 (optionally encrypted) passive advertiser with a GATT config profile and OTA — no Tuya account, no keys, no encryption session. NOTE: the 2026 hardware revision "SGS01B" (different "BTH" module) is NOT yet supported by that project.

openness.notes: Tuya publishes nothing about this category. The transport facts here are corroborated by two independent implementations (python-tuya-ble and the Tuya BLE SDK inside the Smart Life app); the DP maps come from the ha_tuya_ble integration and HA's cloud schema dumps and are marked `reported`, not byte-verified against hardware.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: A factory-fresh or freshly reset tester advertises in pairing mode on its own; the procedure below is for a device that is already bound.

procedures.basis: The vendor quick-start guide for this class of Tuya BLE device. Not replayed against hardware; the exact control differs across the models this spec covers.
procedures.name: Insert batteries, or hold the reset pin, until it advertises in pairing mode

steps.action: Insert the batteries, or hold the reset pin on an already-bound tester.
steps.expect: The tester advertises on Tuya service 0xFD50 in pairing mode.

pairing.notes: Nothing is readable at all without completing this: the session key derives from the device uuid and the cloud-issued local key, so a stock Tuya BLE device is inert to any client that has not paired it. That is the one hard cloud dependency in this spec, and it is one-time — once the device id and local key are extracted, day-to-day local monitoring keeps working with the Tuya cloud gone entirely.

pin.notes: Not a PIN: a device id and 16-character local key, issued by Tuya's cloud during the vendor-app pairing and recoverable afterwards through a Tuya IoT developer project. Per-unit, and rotated whenever the device is unbound and paired again.

unpair.clears: The Tuya account binding and the pairing keys; the device returns to advertising in pairing mode and is issued a new device id and local key on the next pairing.
unpair.notes: Unbinding and factory reset are the same operation on this device, and it is destructive to local access in a way users do not expect: any client holding the old local key stops working, and the replacement key can only be obtained by pairing through the vendor app and cloud again. Moving the tester to a different Tuya account means exactly this — unbind, re-pair, re-extract.

issued_to_client: device id + 16-char local key (recoverable via Tuya IoT developer account + tuya-iot-py-sdk)
credentials.notes: The local key IS the credential for the encrypted BLE session — treat it as a password.
stored_on_device: Tuya device uuid + local_key-derived session keys (issued at pairing)

factory_reset.effect: Unbinds the device from its Tuya account and clears the pairing keys; on re-pairing a new device id / local key pair is issued. The measurement MCU and its calibration are unaffected.

steps.action: Remove the device in the Smart Life / Tuya Smart app (device settings → remove device).
steps.notes: The app drives an UNBIND (function code 0x0005) or DEVICE_RESET (0x0006) frame over GATT; the device returns to advertising in pairing mode. A physical button-hold reset likely exists on the probe's single button (generic Tuya BLE behavior) but is NOT documented for this family — unverified.

steps.action: Flash haraldapp/SGS01BTHome over the BT3L SWS pads (Telink BDT or pvvx TlsrComSwireWriter).
steps.notes: Replaces the whole Tuya stack; afterwards there is no Tuya state to reset. Flash above 0x70000 holds factory MAC/calibration — preserve it. Does not apply to the 2026 SGS01B revision.

methods.description: A stock Tuya BLE device yields nothing until it has been paired: every DP frame afterwards is encrypted with keys derived from the device `uuid` and the cloud-issued `local_key`. So the route has two phases — pair once in Smart Life or Tuya Smart to mint those keys and extract them, then connect directly and run the encrypted session with no hub and no cloud at runtime.
methods.name: Pair once in the vendor app, then run the session yourself

stages.description: Standard Tuya BLE pairing in the vendor app: the device advertises in pairing mode, the app connects over GATT (service 0xFD50), exchanges PAIR frames (function code 0x0001) carrying the cloud-issued credentials, and bonds the device to the Tuya account. Requires a Tuya cloud account in Smart Life or Tuya Smart.
stages.name: Pair in the vendor app, and extract the keys

steps.action: Put the tester in pairing mode (per the vendor quick-start: batteries in / reset pin held) so it advertises on 0xFD50.
Connect over GATT to Tuya service 0xFD50 in the vendor app.
Exchange PAIR frames (function code 0x0001) carrying the cloud-issued credentials, binding the device to the account.
steps.expect: The device appears in Smart Life / Tuya Smart and its uuid and local_key exist in the account.

stages.description: After one-time key extraction (device id + local key via a Tuya IoT developer account), a third-party client connects directly and runs the encrypted session itself — the python-tuya-ble / ha_tuya_ble path. No hub, no cloud at runtime.
stages.name: Run the encrypted session from a third-party client

steps.action: Pair the device once through the vendor app (the ble_provisioning method above); local access needs the credentials that pairing creates.
Fetch the device `uuid` and 16-char `local_key` once from a Tuya IoT developer account (the ha_tuya_ble / tuya-iot-py-sdk flow).
steps.expect: Both secrets in hand; no cloud contact is needed after this.

steps.action: Connect directly and run the encrypted DP session with those keys — no hub and no cloud at runtime.

setup.notes: Unlike a plain BLE sensor, a stock Tuya BLE device must be PAIRED before it yields anything: pairing (in Smart Life / Tuya Smart with a Tuya cloud account) exchanges keys derived from the device `uuid` and the cloud-issued `local_key`, and all subsequent DP traffic is encrypted with them. For third-party local access the same credentials are fetched once from a Tuya IoT developer account (the ha_tuya_ble / tuya-iot-py-sdk flow). Not replayed against this hardware by this project.

rejoin.notes: BLE device — there is no network credential to rotate. Re-binding to a new Tuya account means unbind + re-pair.

testing.notes: No hardware has been exercised by this project. Every fact below is derived from community clean-room work (PlusPlus-ua/python-tuya-ble, garnser/ha_tuya_ble, haraldapp/SGS01BTHome, Home Assistant's Tuya integration) cross-checked against clean-room static analysis of the Smart Life app (see `sources`), whose BLE SDK carries the transport constants and function codes used here. The DP tables are integration-derived and NOT byte-verified against a live device; the Tuya category `zwjcy` has no official public DP schema at all.

variants.notes: Canonical unit (Shenzhen HaiHao Electronic). Tuya category `zwjcy`; current product id. DP map in `dps.table` below. Supported by ha_tuya_ble and by the SGS01BTHome replacement firmware.
Older product id for the same hardware (per Home Assistant discussion #949); works in HA's cloud Tuya integration. DP map presumed identical to gvygg3m8; not independently verified.
Same form factor and DPs, certified under Tuya category `wsdcg` (temperature/humidity sensor) with different DP numbering — see `dps.wsdcg_variants`.

variants.model: wsdcg-category BLE soil tester (alt DP numbering)

variants.notes: New hardware revision with a different ("BTH") radio module, seen in the market in 2026. Uncharacterized: protocol presumed the same Tuya BLE family, but the SGS01BTHome replacement firmware does NOT support it. Treat every fact in this spec as unverified for this revision.

local_access.notes: The Tuya BLE GATT protocol is native local access once the device id + local key are known — direct BLE, no bridge hardware. Home Assistant path: garnser/ha_tuya_ble (HACS), which ships DP maps for gvygg3m8 and the wsdcg variants and uses tuya-iot-py-sdk for key retrieval. The SGS01BTHome firmware-replacement path (BTHome v2 broadcast, optionally encrypted) removes keys and cloud altogether but only covers the SGS01 revision — NOT the 2026 SGS01B.

table.description: Temperature; raw value is tenths of a degree (divide by 10).
°C/°F unit preference. Seen in the cloud schema but not mapped to a BLE DP id in any community source — likely cloud-level only on this product. Unverified.

table.notes: Temperature raw value ÷10, same as the zwjcy map.
No battery DPs documented for this variant.

advertising.notes: Identity only; no sensor readings are ever broadcast.

tuya_ble_protocol.authentication: Pairing (function code 0x0001) establishes session keys derived from the device's Tuya `uuid` and the cloud-issued `local_key`; all DP traffic afterwards is encrypted under them. Key derivation and the crypto layer are implemented in python-tuya-ble (tuya_ble/) — not reproduced here.

dp_types.notes: The classic Tuya DP model carried over BLE: RAW=0x00, BOOL=0x01, VALUE=0x02 (32-bit big-endian), STRING=0x03, ENUM=0x04, BITMAP=0x05. A DP report is a list of [dp id u8][type u8][length u16be][payload].

tuya_ble_protocol.transport: BLE GATT, encrypted session, default ATT MTU 20

tuyamcu_uart.link: UART between BT3L module and sensor MCU (parameters not documented for this unit)
tuyamcu_uart.role: The sensor MCU owns measurement, button and LED; the BT3L module reports the MCU's state as DPs. Factory MAC/calibration live in BT3L flash above 0x70000 — preserve when reflashing.

device_info.description: Query device info (function code 0x0000): device id, product id, firmware version.

dp_query.description: Request current DP values (function code 0x0002; DPS_V4 = 0x0027). Reports arrive on the notify characteristic as 0x8001/0x8006.

pair.description: Pairing handshake (function code 0x0001): exchanges keys derived from the device uuid + cloud-issued local_key. Prerequisite for everything else.

unbind.description: Unbind from the Tuya account (function code 0x0005).

characteristics.name: Write
characteristics.notes: All host→device commands: pairing, DP query/set, device info, unbind/reset, OTA. Byte format is the Tuya BLE encrypted packet (sequence-numbered frames carrying [function code u16be][payload]), chunked at the 20-byte default MTU; the full framing spec lives in python-tuya-ble and is not restated here.

characteristics.name: Notify
characteristics.notes: All device→host traffic: DP reports (function code 0x8001, V4 = 0x8006) carrying the sensor DPs in the `dps` table, time requests (0x8011/0x8012 — answer them or time-dependent features drift), and command responses. Subscribe after pairing; sensor readings only ever arrive here, never in advertisements.

services.name: Tuya BLE service
services.notes: Single custom service carrying the whole Tuya BLE single-point protocol: encrypted framed commands on the write characteristic, encrypted framed responses/reports on the notify characteristic. Default ATT MTU 20; frames are chunked/reassembled by the protocol layer (see python-tuya-ble). Nothing is readable without completing pairing — the session key comes from the device uuid + cloud local key.
